evidence.title: I’m running an Opus-level coding agent locally at nearly 2x Claude Opus speed, for free.

name: I’m running an Opus-level coding agent locally at nearly 2x Claude Opus speed
summary: Julian Harris post on running a local Opus-level coding agent with Qwen 3.8 27B: benchmarks, quantization and speed boosts.
description: Hand-written long-form post (Sep 4, 2026) in the AI Local newsletter on replacing commercial coding agents with local AI: why local models became viable, quants and fine-tune behaviour changes, prediction boosts (MTP and DFlash), cache boosts such as TurboQuant, thinking time, kernel optimisations and thermal throttling on Macs, then the tested stacks at 128k context — Ubuntu with an RTX 4090 24GB and a MacBook Pro M5 Max 128GB, both close to 2x Claude Opus speed against a 40 tokens/second baseline.
contains: published Sep 4, 2026 by Julian Harris; hand-written long-form
Ubuntu with RTX 4090 24GB: nearly 2x Claude Opus speed
MacBook Pro M5 Max 128GB: also nearly 2x Opus
topics: quants and fine-tunes, MTP and DFlash, TurboQuant, thinking time, kernel optimisations, thermal throttling
AI Local is a reader-supported publication with free and paid tiers
